intended_object: Galois descent of algebra morphisms. Let L/k be a Galois extension. An L-algebra map F : L ⊗_k A → L ⊗_k B that commutes with the Galois action σ ⊗ id comes from a unique k-algebra map f : A → B with id_L ⊗ f = F (Milne, Algebraic Groups, A.64). I took this from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
How it is built: for a ∈ A, the element F(1 ⊗ a) is fixed by every σ ⊗ id. This follows from the hypothesis hF, using that σ ⊗ id fixes 1 ⊗ a. By the lemma just above the definition, the elements of L ⊗_k B fixed by all σ are exactly those of the form 1 ⊗ b. That lemma uses the infinite Galois fixed-field theorem and a basis of B over k. The map a ↦ F(1 ⊗ a) therefore lands in the image of includeRight. Since L/k is a field extension, includeRight is injective, so composing with the inverse of the isomorphism B ≃ image gives a k-algebra map A → B.

Checks: the library proves that one_tmul_galoisDescend gives 1 ⊗ f(a) = F(1 ⊗ a). It proves that map_galoisDescend recovers F as id ⊗ f. It also proves uniqueness and that the equivariance condition characterises existence (existsUnique_map_eq_iff). So the definition gives exactly the descended morphism.

Generality: A and B are arbitrary k-algebras, so noncommutative semirings are allowed. L/k may be any Galois extension, including infinite ones. This is the standard setting for Galois descent. One could weaken the condition on L to only requiring that the fixed field of Aut(L/k) be k, but Galois is the setting used in the literature. Mathlib has no counterpart; a search for descent/descend in Mathlib/FieldTheory found nothing.
